note.text: Adverbs of frequency say how often an action happens. Always indicates every relevant occasion; usually and often indicate frequent occurrence; sometimes is less regular; never means no occasions. Their exact numerical frequency is not fixed. A common position is before an ordinary main verb but after be: Bih often reads; Bih is often early. Some adverbs allow other positions. Do not mark a different standard position wrong merely because it is not the model's preferred pattern.

sections.heading: Understand the ideas
sections.text: Adverbs of frequency say how often an action happens. Always indicates every relevant occasion; usually and often indicate frequent occurrence; sometimes is less regular; never means no occasions. Their exact numerical frequency is not fixed. A common position is before an ordinary main verb but after be: Bih often reads; Bih is often early. Some adverbs allow other positions. Do not mark a different standard position wrong merely because it is not the model's preferred pattern.

sections.heading: Apply the ideas locally
sections.text: Bih usually studies after chores, but sometimes she studies at the library. Ayuk is often early for the reading club. These sentences describe habits, not how fast or carefully the learners work. A timetable can help a learner report a habit accurately rather than claiming always after one observed occasion.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Ask whether the word concerns frequency, manner or time. For the simple pattern, place it before an ordinary main verb and after be. Keep the meaning when changing word order. Never is already negative in standard school usage: avoid adding an unnecessary not.
